Every province's zone rows sum EXACTLY to its Table 1 total (Ituri 2646/1107 across 28 named zones, Nord-Kivu 290/182 across 11, Haut-Uele 29/15 across 5, Tshopo 5/4 across 3, Sud-Kivu 3/1 across 1) and the five provinces sum exactly to the printed national 2973/1309 with no residual. This is the normal case, and it is worth stating explicitly because the previous cycle was not: SitRep69 restated its cumulative by +369 against 97 notified after integrating harmonized provincial databases. lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 155 samples documented in the collection network / 51 positive (33 living, 18 deaths) = 32.9%; Nord-Kivu 120 received and analyzed / 15 positive (7 living, 8 deaths) = 12.5%; Tshopo 3 received and analyzed, ALL negative, so Tshopo contributes 3 to the denominator and 0 to the numerator rather than being excluded. Positivity uses 66 positives over 278 analyzed samples across three provinces = 23.7%. Haut-Uele and Sud-Kivu report no laboratory block this cycle and are excluded rather than counted as zero. IMPORTANT: the day's laboratory positives (51 + 15 + 0 = 66) do NOT equal the day's 68 confirmations, unlike every recent cycle. The 2-case difference is exactly Haut-Uele's two notified cases (Rungu 1, Wamba 1), which have no corresponding laboratory line because the province reports no lab block; the identity holds once Haut-Uele is accounted for (66 + 2 = 68). Testing volume contracted 414 -> 278 analyzed (-33%) and the reporting denominator narrowed from four provinces to three, so the positivity move is a volume and composition effect, not a prevalence signal. A new diagnostic laboratory was installed and launched at Kasenyi (Tchomia health zone, Ituri) under DRC-Uganda cross-border coordination with WHO and US CDC support, including two WHO-supplied RadiOne machines.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 23/07): 1531 alerts of the day (1483 new + 48 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Tshopo; Haut-Uele and Sud-Kivu are ND on every alert row and are excluded from the denominators rather than counted as zero. Province rows sum exactly (550+948+33 = 1531 reported; 296+917+9 = 1222 investigated; 137+64+8 = 209 living; 62+43+1 = 106 community deaths; 199+107+9 = 315 suspects, and 209 + 106 = 315). The national rate 1222/1531 = 79.8% is essentially flat against SitRep69's 79.5% and MASKS a severe epicentre collapse: Ituri fell 64.0% -> 53.8% (296/550), leaving 254 alerts uninvestigated, a SIXTH consecutive cycle of decline across 86.4 -> 75.6 -> 72.8 -> 66.7 -> 64.0 -> 53.8, while Nord-Kivu ROSE 87.1% -> 96.7% and carries the national figure. Tshopo also fell hard, 86.7% -> 27.3% (9/33) on a small denominator. The source narrative again describes the movement as an improvement reflecting reduced investigation carry-over; that reading is preserved but it conflicts with the printed Ituri and Tshopo rates.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of responders (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; resumption announced after the intervention of Ituri's military governor) interrupts response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise responder payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy 136.2% in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 80.4% in Ituri (570 patients for 709 beds), raising admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance remains weak: Ituri 72.1%, Nord-Kivu 78.9%, both far below the 95% operational target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted; the source again asks to investigate the fall observed in Ituri.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision; investigate the Ituri decline.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points cause transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%) drive high nosocomial infection risk, with 123 first-line personnel infected and 36 dead. The infected count rose from 121 at SitRep69 while deaths held at 36.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) and high mobility raise the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion. Rungu (Haut-Uele) becomes the 48th affected health zone this cycle.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Installation of proximity laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) is incomplete, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilisation and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services is compromised, raising indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of essential-service continuity.

priorities.priority: Contain Rungu (Haut-Uele) at first detection: 1 confirmed case notified this cycle, taking Haut-Uele to 5 affected zones. Rungu needs its own GRID3 v8.0 centroid and must not be collapsed into a neighbouring zone. Establish alert, contact and laboratory reporting there, none of which Haut-Uele currently provides.

Nord-Kivu isolation saturation is the acute emergency: 136.2% (192 of 141 beds), worsened from 119.1% and a series high, reversing last cycle's improvement. Ituri rose 77.7% -> 80.4% on flat 709 beds. Restore ND bed reporting in Haut-Uele.

Ituri alert investigation collapsed to 53.8% (296/550), a sixth consecutive decline leaving 254 alerts uninvestigated, while the national 79.8% held flat only because Nord-Kivu rose to 96.7%. Tshopo also fell to 27.3%. Restore Haut-Uele and Sud-Kivu alert reporting, ND on every row.
Ituri contact follow-up fell a third consecutive cycle to 72.1%; Nord-Kivu recovered slightly to 78.9%. Both remain far below the 95% target and the national decline is Ituri's alone.

Testing volume contracted 414 -> 278 analyzed (-33%) and the reporting denominator narrowed from four provinces to three, so read positivity as volume and composition, not prevalence. Consolidate the new Kasenyi laboratory (Tchomia, Ituri) opened under DRC-Uganda cross-border coordination, and restore a Haut-Uele block: its two notified cases this cycle have no laboratory line.
Community deaths were 26 of 40 confirmed deaths (65.0%), with Ituri at 18 of 30 (60.0%). The post-mortem share of confirmations was 26 of 68 (38.2%).

preserved_conflicts: SitRep70 national headline is DRC-only (2973 confirmed / 1309 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 2993 confirmed / 1311 deaths / 551 recovered. Uganda MoH reports no new cases through 2026-07-23 against a cumulative of 20 (last positive 2026-06-21), so the anchor is carried unchanged on a confirmed rather than an assumed basis.

NO HARMONIZATION this cycle, in explicit contrast to SitRep69. SitRep70 frames its movement as ordinary 24h notification (+68 cases, +40 deaths, +21 recoveries) and the cumulative is cleanly additive (2905 + 68 = 2973; 1269 + 40 = 1309). The count-reconciliation gate classifies both metrics as reconciled, so this boundary IS safe to difference.

Nord-Kivu bed occupancy: Tableau 6 prints 136,2% while the section-4 narrative prints 135,5% for the same 192 patients over 141 beds. 192/141 = 136.17%, so the tabled 136.2% is arithmetically correct and is promoted; the narrative 135.5% is preserved as a source slip.

The day's laboratory positives (51 + 15 + 0 = 66) do NOT equal the day's 68 confirmations. The 2-case difference is exactly Haut-Uele's two notified cases (Rungu 1, Wamba 1), which carry no laboratory line because the province reports no lab block this cycle. Preserved rather than forced: the identity holds at 66 + 2 = 68.

The section-3.1 alert narrative describes the movement as 'cette amelioration' reflecting reduced investigation carry-over, but Ituri fell 64.0% -> 53.8% and Tshopo fell 86.7% -> 27.3%; only Nord-Kivu rose. The printed rates are promoted and the narrative characterisation preserved as a source conflict.

Zone-name variance between the page-1 roster and Tableau 2 persists: the roster prints 'Gety' and 'Nia-Nia' where Tableau 2 prints 'Gethy' and 'Nia Nia'. The LOVS canonical slugs (Gety, Nia-Nia) are promoted for series continuity.

PoE/PoC totals are summed from per-province prose (Ituri 5, Nord-Kivu 5, Tshopo 0) because SitRep70 does not print a single tabled global alert column this cycle; they are labelled prose-derived rather than tabled.

Wamba revises 6 -> 7 confirmed with 1 notified in the day column, and Bambu's deaths revise 9 -> 10 with 1 intra-CTE death notified, so both are ordinary same-cycle movements rather than restatements.
